page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, which is bundled directly with the instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the compute and memory performance of the i3.xlarge is relatively modest compared to modern standards. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of performance. Similarly, memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as large block read and write operations, fall into the bottom 10% category. Geekbench scores for single-core and multi-core tasks, along with software compilation and text processing, also register in the bottom 10%, while Passmark CPU and memory scores are categorized as weak (bottom 25%).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i3.xlarge trades high-performance compute capabilities for high local storage density and capacity. The value proposition of this hardware profile lies in its local NVMe SSD storage rather than raw processing power or memory speed. Consequently, this instance is best suited for workloads that require fast local storage access but have low CPU demands, such as local database caching, basic NoSQL databases, or storage-heavy development environments.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for workloads requiring high local storage capacity. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, it provides 4 vCPUs, 30.0 GB of RAM, and a dedicated 950 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the Xen hypervisor, the instance features a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates that compute and memory performance are modest, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and memory bandwidth tests consistently placing in the bottom 10% to 25% of results. Given these performance characteristics, the i3.xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-dense applications rather than compute-intensive tasks. It is best suited for workloads such as local database operations, basic web serving, and storage-heavy development environments where high-speed local NVMe storage is prioritized over raw processing power.
